subject.title: [Feature]: Inbound media shared across all agents — no per-agent isolation

question: What identity should OpenClaw use as the durable inbound-media isolation boundary across save, resolve, stage, cleanup, and plugin APIs?
rationale: The source proves the shared flat pool remains, but choosing account, resolved agent, session, channel/chat, tenant, or indexed provenance is a security and compatibility decision automation should not invent.

options.title: Adopt scoped managed media contract
options.body: Define a core contract for scoped managed inbound media, then update bundled channels, resolvers, staging, cleanup, docs, and tests together.

options.title: Limit first step to account subdirs
options.body: Use sanitized channel/account identifiers as the first isolation boundary, accepting that session/chat/tenant provenance remains follow-up work.

options.title: Defer for media provenance design
options.body: Keep the tracker open until maintainers choose a broader media index or provenance schema for filesystem and resolver behavior.

recommendation.title: Adopt scoped managed media contract
recommendation.body: Define a core contract for scoped managed inbound media, then update bundled channels, resolvers, staging, cleanup, docs, and tests together.

likelyOwner.reason: The history most strongly routes the original inbound media and sandbox-staging contracts through this area.
